title: WeatherAPI — Keys in the Open
objective: WeatherAPI accepts your key as a query parameter for convenience. Find out where that choice leaves a trace, then use what you find there.

verifier.condition: A weather request succeeds using an API key that was never issued to the caller, obtained from the request log.

weakness: Accepting the API key as a query parameter means it becomes part of the full request URL, and a separate request-log feature records full URLs verbatim, so anyone who can read that log can recover any key sent this way.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /api/weather?key=... then GET /api/request-log (records full URLs including query strings)
seededData: Two issued API keys, one for a 'demo' partner and a separate, more privileged 'internal-tools' key. In-memory request log.
hints: Make a weather request with your own demo key and see what it returns.
This API offers a request log, seemingly for debugging. What does an entry in it actually contain?
Someone else's request appears in that same log, with their key in it.
burpNotes: Fetch /api/request-log directly and look for another caller's full request URL, including its query string.
